_comment: real device-code logins (public client CLI) — one against the test instance, one against
production. NO TOKEN IS RECORDED HERE: only claim NAMES, and the few claim VALUES that
define the verifier's accept criteria. `sub` is the measuring user's own login.
This file is the authority for BfabricOidc::TokenVerifier's accept criteria. The OIDC
discovery document is NOT: its `claims_supported` over-promises (it lists `groups` and
`containers`, both of which are delivered nowhere) AND under-promises (it lists neither
`client_id` nor `azp`, yet the access token carries `client_id`). Measure, do not infer.

audience_narrows_to_the_api_not_to_us: `aud` is the literal string API on BOTH instances. Every B-Fabric API token carries it,
so it separates an access token from an id_token (aud=CLI) but does NOT separate a token
minted for New SUSHI from one minted for any other B-Fabric relying party. Asking for a
resource indicator (RFC 8707) or a SUSHI-specific aud remains open question 2.
client_id_makes_the_allow_list_real: `client_id` IS present, contradicting the inference drawn from `claims_supported`.
BFABRIC_OIDC_ALLOWED_CLIENT_IDS=CLI is therefore enforceable and is the ONLY narrowing
available today. Its limit, stated plainly: CLI is the PUBLIC client anyone may drive,
so the allow-list blocks a token minted for a DIFFERENT B-Fabric client and does not
block someone who deliberately uses CLI. Add the confidential client's id to the list
when the browser path is registered.
id_token_is_doubly_excluded: An id_token presented where an access token belongs now fails twice over: its aud is CLI,
not API, and it carries at_hash which the access token never does.
issuer_needs_no_pinning: `iss` equals the base URL exactly on both instances, so BFABRIC_OIDC_ISSUER can stay
unset and the discovery document's own `issuer` is used.
ldap_still_supplies_membership: Neither groups nor containers appears in the access token, the id_token or /userinfo.
device_code_works_on_production: The public client CLI is registered for the device_code grant on PRODUCTION as well as
test. This closes one of the seven questions for the B-Fabric team.
